questions.text: What is the minimum number of 2-input NOR gates required to implement 4-variable function expressed in sum-of-minterms from as [latex]f = \Sigma (0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15)[/latex]? Assume that all the inputs and their complements are available. Answer ________ .
questions.solution:
K-map: minterms 0, 2, 8, 10 = [latex]\bar B\bar D[/latex] and 5, 7, 13, 15 = BD. So [latex]f=BD+\bar B\bar D[/latex] (XNOR of B and D).

In product-of-sums form: [latex]f=(B+\bar D)(\bar B+D)[/latex]. With NOR gates:
- [latex]G_1=NOR(B,\bar D)[/latex], [latex]G_2=NOR(\bar B,D)[/latex]
- [latex]f=NOR(G_1,G_2)=(B+\bar D)(\bar B+D)[/latex]

3 gates (complements are available).

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Consider three 4-variable functions [latex]f_1,f_2 \; and \; f_3[/latex], which are expressed in sum-of-minterms

[latex]f_1=\Sigma (0,2,5,8,14)[/latex]
[latex]f_2=\Sigma (2,3,6,8,14,15)[/latex]
[latex]f_3=\Sigma (2,7,11,14)[/latex]

For the following circuit with one AND gate and one XOR gate, the output function f can be expressed as:
questions.solution:
Circuit: [latex]f=(f_1\cdot f_2)\oplus f_3[/latex].

- [latex]f_1\cdot f_2[/latex] = common minterms = {2, 8, 14}
- XOR with [latex]f_3[/latex] = {2, 7, 11, 14}: keep minterms in exactly one set [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 and 14 cancel, leaving {7, 8, 11}

Answer: [latex]\Sigma(7,8,11)[/latex]

questions.text: Consider Z = X - Y where X, Y and Z are all in sign-magnitude form. X and Y are each represented in n bits. To avoid overflow, the representation of Z would require a minimum of:
questions.solution:
In sign-magnitude, n bits give 1 sign bit and n [latex]-[/latex] 1 magnitude bits. X [latex]-[/latex] Y can be as large as (max magnitude) + (max magnitude), e.g. (+max) [latex]-[/latex] ([latex]-[/latex]max), which needs one more magnitude bit.

So Z needs n + 1 bits.

Answer: n+1 bits

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT a valid identity?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- XOR is associative [latex]\text{---}[/latex] valid.
- Take x = 1, y = 1, z = 0: [latex](x+y)\oplus z=1\oplus0=1[/latex] but [latex]x\oplus(y+z)=1\oplus1=0[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not valid.
- If xy = 0, x and y are never both 1, so XOR equals OR [latex]\text{---}[/latex] valid.
- [latex]xy+x'y'[/latex] is XNOR; its complement is XOR [latex]\text{---}[/latex] valid.

Answer: [latex](x+y)\oplus z=x\oplus(y+z)[/latex]

questions.text: In 16-bit 2's complement representation, the decimal number -28 is:
questions.solution:
+28 in 16 bits = 0000 0000 0001 1100.
2's complement: invert [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1111 1111 1110 0011, add 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1111 1111 1110 0100.

Answer: 1111 1111 1110 0100
